$comment: The registry of slices and their requirement-code prefixes. Each slice is one OpenSpec capability: a folder under openspec/specs/ (and under a change's specs/). Every requirement in it is coded <code>-<n>, numbered in order and never renumbered. A new slice is added here first. tools/check_spec_ids.py enforces this registry; openspec/README.md shows it as a table and the docs site's Requirements page lists every requirement by slice.

slices.title: Architecture
slices.summary: How the system is built and what it stores.
slices.description: The two-container shape of bundlemcp (a Python gateway serving MCP endpoints, OAuth and the management API, and an optional Nuxt admin app), the stack and version policy, and the state model behind the restart-safety promise: Postgres for everything durable, a RESP store (Valkey) for everything live, and no in-memory-only state a request depends on. It also defines the persisted entities, their naming rules, cascades and secret-bearing columns, and the package layout with its layer rules.
slices.boundary: Behaviour that clients observe lives in the feature slices; this slice holds the structural rules they all rely on.

slices.title: Documentation
slices.summary: What people read to run, use and change bundlemcp.
slices.description: The user-facing documentation site (self-hosting, managing, connecting clients, integrating), the repository README and the demo seed that makes a fresh install useful. It also owns the architecture documentation: arc42 sections, append-only ADRs, the LikeC4 model as the single source of diagrams, and the rule that docs and decisions land in the same pull request as the behaviour they describe.
slices.boundary: What the gateway does is specified in the other slices; this slice specifies how it is documented and where.

slices.title: Upstreams
slices.summary: The upstream MCP servers the gateway proxies, and how it reaches them.
slices.description: Registering an upstream server (Streamable HTTP only, with inspection that pre-fills a registration), its connection settings and health, the egress policy every request to it passes, and discovering and caching its tools in Postgres so bundles can be curated while it is down. It also covers authenticating to upstreams: static headers, OAuth with tokens held per user or shared, the interactive connect flow, refresh on 401, and introspection for forwarded bearers.
slices.boundary: How an upstream's tools are presented in a bundle is the bundles slice; the caller's identity forwarded to an upstream is the auth slice.

slices.title: Bundles
slices.summary: Composing upstreams into one virtual MCP server, and curating what it presents.
slices.description: A bundle combines several upstreams under one set of prefixed, collision-free tool names and routes each call back to its owner. Per bundle, an admin decides which tools are shown and how: enable flags, name, title, description and annotation overrides. A bundle can also carry prompts and resources of its own, written by an admin and served without contacting any upstream, beside the members' prompts and resources, which pass through live. The catalogue overview a user reads before connecting belongs here too.
slices.boundary: Where a bundle is reachable, by whom and with which client quirks is the endpoints slice.

slices.title: Endpoints
slices.summary: The public URLs that serve a bundle, each shaped for one kind of client.
slices.description: One bundle can have many endpoints, each with its own URL, accepted authentication modes (OAuth, API key, none), profile and rate limits. Profiles adapt the tool surface to a client's quirks: claude, chatgpt (which re-annotates write tools so ChatGPT accepts them) and default. Rate limits hold across all replicas through shared counters, answer 429 with Retry-After, and include the limiter on authentication failures.
slices.boundary: How a credential is issued and validated is the auth slice; what the endpoint serves is the bundles and protocol slices.

slices.title: Authentication and identity
slices.summary: Who may call the gateway, and who the upstreams learn the caller is.
slices.description: The built-in OAuth 2.1 authorization server for MCP clients (discovery, dynamic and metadata-document client registration, PKCE, consent, endpoint-bound tokens, introspection and revocation), OIDC-only login for admins and users with roles taken from the identity provider, API keys for scripts and services, and identity forwarding: selected client headers, the X-MCP-User header and delegated tokens that tell an upstream who is calling.
slices.boundary: Authenticating the gateway to an upstream with the upstream's own OAuth is the upstreams slice.

slices.title: Sessions
slices.summary: Live state that any replica can serve, and keeping every replica's view current.
slices.description: Handshake-era MCP sessions are records in the RESP store, so any replica serves them and a restart loses nothing; modern-era requests are stateless. Live streams are pinned to the replica holding them, and messages reach them from any replica over pub/sub. The degradation matrix says what happens when the RESP store or Postgres is down. Configuration changes publish invalidation events, so caches on every replica are flushed within a two-second budget.
slices.boundary: The MCP messages carried over a session are the protocol slice.

slices.title: Protocol
slices.summary: The MCP surface the gateway speaks to clients and upstreams.
slices.description: bundlemcp is a bidirectional proxy, not a tools-only router: it relays progress, cancellation, logging, completions, list-changed notifications and the upstream's requests for client input, across protocol revisions (the session-based handshake era and the stateless 2026-07-28 era) with one dialect per revision. Every tool call runs through a fixed pipeline (curation, profile, metering, audit), and the metering hook is the supported, versioned extension point where an application layer plugs in billing.
slices.boundary: Session storage and cross-replica delivery are the sessions slice; what is recorded per call is the operations slice.

slices.title: Management
slices.description: The versioned management REST API under /api/v1 (the admin UI uses nothing else, so everything is automatable), authenticated by admin session or service key, with its DTOs, pagination, retry-safe writes and browser-facing protections. Bootstrap provisions upstreams, bundles and endpoints idempotently from a document at startup, through the same code paths as the API. Export and import move the whole configuration between gateways as that same document, secrets as placeholders.
slices.boundary: The UI on top of this API is the admin-ui slice.

slices.title: Operations
slices.summary: What operators see while the gateway runs.
slices.description: The append-only audit log: one record per tool call (who, what, where, how long, how it ended), denied calls included, never arguments or results, written asynchronously without slowing calls, queryable through the API and UI, and the reconciliation source for an application layer's billing. Structured logs and the health and readiness probes for orchestrators. Metrics, tracing and the live log view will live here once built.
slices.boundary: Rate-limit and lockout counters are specified with their limiters in the endpoints slice.

slices.title: Admin UI
slices.summary: The admin app, and the catalogue signed-in users see.
slices.description: A Nuxt single-page app that is a pure client of the management API, with types generated from its OpenAPI document: pages for upstreams (with guided registration), bundles and curation, endpoints and their connection cards, API keys, users and consents, audit and settings, and a catalogue showing a signed-in non-admin what they can connect to. The built-in inspector will live here once built.
slices.boundary: Every action the UI offers is specified as API behaviour in the management slice and the feature slices.

slices.title: Security
slices.summary: The threat model and the controls the other slices rely on.
slices.description: One egress policy for every request the gateway makes to an admin-supplied or remotely named URL, and its defaults against SSRF (blocked metadata and loopback ranges, allowed private networks); CORS and CSRF rules for the management API; hardening of the OAuth browser pages; request size limits; limits against dynamic client registration abuse; lockout after authentication failures; and the rule that secrets never appear in logs, responses or audit records.
slices.boundary: Feature slices reference these controls instead of re-deriving them.

slices.title: Deployment
slices.summary: Running bundlemcp in production and upgrading it safely.
slices.description: The public URL as the single source of the gateway's identity behind a reverse proxy, trusted proxies and the client IP, the reference topology and health checks, migrations as a guarded step that stays backward compatible one release back, versioned session records so rolling upgrades work, backup and restore, rotation of the token encryption keys, and the CI gates and image publishing that deliver it.
slices.boundary: Configuration settings themselves are documented per feature; this slice is the operational contract.

former_codes.$comment: Codes published before the slices were consolidated on 2026-10-13, and the code each one has now.
